exposure: Children of mothers who received oxytocin
Children of mothers who did not receive oxytocin
outcome: Developmental delay at age 5, assessed using the Battelle Developmental Inventory
cohort: 148 children born at a maternity ward in 2006
finding: While oxytocin use during delivery did not significantly affect the overall risk of developmental delay at age 5, it increased the risk in vaginal deliveries for mothers younger than 28 or older than 35, but decreased the risk in instrumental or cesarean deliveries for mothers aged 28-35.
mod_finding: Oxytocin administration during delivery was associated with an increased risk of developmental delay in vaginal deliveries for mothers outside the age range of 28-35, but a decreased risk in instrumental or cesarean deliveries for mothers aged 28-35.
